title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1971-02-21
lineage: Jace's DAT (48 KHz) playback on Sony PCM-R500, AES digital output > Benchmark DAC1, XLR analog output > Grace Lunatec V3, sample rate at 96 KHz, AES digiout) > AES digital input, professional mode/sync - LynxTwo soundcard in E6400 dual core processor-based PC > HD as 24 bit/96 KHz WAV > Ozone 3.0 > MBIT+ dithering to 16/44.1 KHz WAV > CDWAV 1.9 (tracking) > FLAC (level 8).   Recording, editing and mastering with Wavelab 5.0.  All cables were Mogami Gold 0.3m pro-audio XLR cables.  All components in the transfer/mastering chain were powered from a Cyberpower 1285AVR noise-attenuated uninterruptible AC power supply.
taper: Original WBOTB DATs procured & circulated in 1996 by Jace Crouch and Tim Deibert. Thanks to trailmix for providing the lineaged master DAT  for transfer.
source: 7" two track BBD reel w/ Dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) > PCM501ES analog out > Dolby A decoder > Apogee filter > analog in PCMF1/PCM501ES analog out > Fostex D5 @ 48 kHz > WBOTB Master DAT (DAT-1).

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a solid early‑70s run, with standout performances of Loser, Easy Wind and the China/Rider segue, though some mid‑set moments lag.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crisp, clear soundboard quality, even if Jerry’s guitar can be buried in the first half while Bob Weir sits front‑and‑center. The show delivers solid energy with high points on Loser, Easy Wind, China/Rider and a tight Good Lovin' finale, though a few songs (e.g., Ripple) fall short of the band’s usual brilliance.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show and recording highly; the performance is solid with notable highlights, and the soundboard source is described as clear and crisp with only minor mix issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as clear, crisp and intact; some reviewers note a slight mix imbalance (Jerry buried early, Weir prominent) but overall an excellent soundboard capture.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts strong through Easy Wind, then loses steam before a high‑energy closing GSET > JBG; second set opens well with China/Rider and Bird Song, runs average in the middle, and finishes strong with Good Lovin'.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar tones praised and leads described as punchy, though his presence is buried in the first half of the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar shines, sitting front‑and‑center in the mix and driving the groove throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann carries the band with solid, driving playing after Mickey’s absence; his drumming is highlighted on Easy Wind and Good Lovin'.
